title: Summary, review and chapter test
competency: Review the unit and take the timed chapter test.

keywords.def: The total amount all sectors (households, firms, government, foreigners) are ready to spend on an economy's goods and services in a period: AD = C + I + G + (X − M).
The quantity supplied of all goods and services (real GDP) at various price levels, other things equal.
The price level and real GDP at which real GDP demanded equals real GDP supplied: where AD meets AS.

en.text: Aggregate demand is total planned spending, AD = C + I + G + (X − M); the AD curve slopes down and shifts when spending changes at a given price level. Aggregate supply is real GDP supplied at each price level; SRAS slopes up, LRAS is vertical at natural real GDP, and input prices, resources, technology, taxes and weather shift SRAS. AD and AS together determine equilibrium output and the price level; demand shocks move them the same way, supply shocks opposite ways.

am.text: AD = C + I + G + (X − M)። SRAS ወደ ላይ፣ LRAS ቀጥ ያለ ነው። የAD እና AS መገናኛ ሚዛናዊ ምርትንና ዋጋን ይወስናል።

screens.title: Unit summary
paras: Aggregate demand: total spending by households, firms and government; AD = C + I + G + (X − M).
The AD curve slopes down. Determinants: income, the real interest rate, foreign activity, credit, home activity.
Aggregate supply: real GDP supplied at various price levels. Determinants: input prices, resources, technology, business taxes and subsidies, weather.
SRAS slopes up; LRAS is vertical.
AD and AS together determine equilibrium national output and the price level.

screens.title: Key words
defs: The total amount all sectors (households, firms, government, foreigners) are ready to spend on an economy's goods and services in a period: AD = C + I + G + (X − M).
The quantity supplied of all goods and services (real GDP) at various price levels, other things equal.
The price level and real GDP at which real GDP demanded equals real GDP supplied: where AD meets AS.

screens.text: The interaction of AD and AS determines
opts: equilibrium national output and the price level
screens.ans: equilibrium national output and the price level
screens.why: p.46: "Interaction between AD and AS determines the equilibrium level of national output and price level."

screens.text: A higher real interest rate is one reason AD shifts to the right.
screens.why: A higher real interest rate lowers I and C, so AD shifts LEFT. The summary lists the real interest rate as a determinant; its direction is reversed.
screens.clue: Think of loans for houses and machines.

screens.title: Match each curve with its shape
screens.clue: Which one ignores the price level?

screens.text: The Birr depreciates and, at the same time, imported fuel becomes dearer. Which is certain?
screens.why: Depreciation raises NX, so AD shifts right (P ↑, Y ↑). Dearer fuel shifts SRAS left (P ↑, Y ↓). Both push P up; the effect on Y depends on sizes.
screens.clue: Find each shift and its effect on P and Y.

items.text: When the price level falls, the real value of money rises and spending increases. This is called
items.why: The book calls it the real balance effect (p.28), also known as the wealth effect.
items.clue: It works through the money people hold.

items.text: An increase in government spending, all else the same, shifts AD from the initial curve AD₀ to
opts: neither curve, because G does not affect AD
items.why: G is part of AD = C + I + G + (X − M); more G shifts AD right. "All else the same" means taxes do not change.

items.text: In the short run, lower aggregate demand will cause
opts: a large decrease in the price level, but no change in output
a lower price level, but only a slight decrease in output
a lower level of output, but only a slight decrease in the price level
a large decrease in both the price level and output
items.ans: a lower level of output, but only a slight decrease in the price level
items.why: In the short run wages and prices are sticky, so SRAS is fairly flat: a fall in AD mostly cuts output.
items.clue: Sticky prices adjust only a little.

items.text: Which one is a determinant of aggregate demand?
opts: general level of income of the people
items.why: All three are in the book's list (p.29).

items.text: Everything else held constant, aggregate demand increases when
items.why: Lower taxes raise disposable income (C ↑) and after-tax profit (I ↑). Less G or less money lowers AD.

items.ask: C = 600, I = 150, G = 200, X = 120, M = 170 (billion Birr). AD = ___ billion Birr
Qd = 1000 − 200P and Qs = 200 + 200P. The equilibrium price level is ___

items.text: A change in aggregate quantity demanded is
opts: a movement along AD caused by a change in the price level
a shift of AD caused by lower taxes
a shift of AD caused by higher foreign incomes
items.ans: a movement along AD caused by a change in the price level
items.why: Price level → movement; anything else → shift.

items.text: A change in aggregate supply (not quantity supplied) is caused by
opts: a change in the price level
items.why: Non-price factors such as wages shift SRAS (Figure 2.4). A price-level change moves along it.

test.text: Which effect explains why AD slopes down?
A storm destroys crops. SRAS shifts
Nominal wage 36 Birr and price index 1.20. The real wage is
Which pair moves the price level and real GDP in OPPOSITE directions?
opts: A rise in oil prices; new technology
A tax cut; more government spending
A rise in foreign incomes; a tax cut
Less government spending; a tax rise
test.ans: A rise in oil prices; new technology

notes.text: Part I Q1: options are lettered E–H instead of A–D, and the stem reads "because of the increases the real value of money". The lesson drops the letters and rewords the stem.
Part I Q3: the answer (C) needs the idea that short-run prices are sticky (a fairly flat SRAS), which the book explains only for wages. Teachers may want to state this assumption.
Unit summary (p.45) repeats the real interest rate as an AD determinant without its direction: a higher real interest rate shifts AD left.
Part II Q2–Q3 use the added worked numbers so they can be checked; the book asks for explanation and a diagram. The chapter test draws from the section tests.
